C_judge.reasoning_summary: All five solvers agree criterion (a) was met: 20 Starlink V3 satellites deployed successfully on Flight 13 (July 24, 2026). The dispute is over criterion (b), the Super Heavy booster landing. Four solvers cite specific, detailed and mutually consistent evidence (Wikipedia's Flight 13 article, The Register, NASASpaceflight, Spaceflight Now, SpaceNews, starship fandom wiki) that Booster 20's landing burn failed — only ~10 of 13 Raptors relit, dropping to ~5 firing at splashdown — resulting in a hard impact and destruction of the booster. B1's YES rests largely on the Space.com headline about the 'softest splashdown ever', which B3 persuasively identifies as referring to the Starship upper stage, not the booster; B1's own cited Register/CNN coverage is characterized elsewhere as 'mostly successful'/'faced hurdles', consistent with a booster landing failure. The resolution criteria explicitly state a failed landing burn or destruction on impact resolves NO even with successful deployment. The minority YES appears to be a conflation of ship and booster outcomes.

All five solvers agree on the underlying facts and cite the same authoritative sources: TRM Labs, Galaxy Research, Forbes, CBC, TechCrunch, BleepingComputer and The Hacker News documented that a firmware build-flag error in Coinkite's COLDCARD hardware wallet caused seed generation to fall back to a weak software PRNG (entropy collapsing from 128 bits to ~40 bits), and that attackers drained roughly 1,816 BTC (~$116M, some outlets reporting up to $130M) from thousands of addresses across four waves between July 30 and early August 2026 — all documented well before the August 15, 2026 deadline. Every element of the resolution criteria (security researchers + blockchain analytics firms, >$100M, hardware wallet firmware weak pseudorandom seed generation, documented by the deadline) is met. The only disagreement is B5's hyper-literal reading of "within a calendar month" as requiring the entire cumulative total to fall inside a single named month (July or August). That reading is not supported by the criteria's plain purpose: the phrase specifies a one-month time window for accumulation, and the entire theft occurred within roughly a six-day span — comfortably inside any one-month window. B5 itself concedes the substantive elements are satisfied. The majority position also has better-grounded evidence tying the $100M+ figure to analytics-firm documentation before the deadline.
